history.position: THIS COURSE TEACHES NO REPAIR HISTORY. The engine's review changes (the exact refusal wordings, the stated quantile rule) landed before its merge and before any lesson was written; they are provenance. The digest describes the engine as it is.

scopeSeams.Arps decline curves: OWNED BY the decline curve analysis course (dca). D4 imports fitArpsModel as a baseline, prints what the engine returns (model, qi, Di per month, b) and never re-derives the equations.
scopeSeams.regression, splits by whole wells and k-: OWNED BY D2 mlcore. D4 teaches the rolling origin, the time-series form of an honest test, and names the well-by-well split with a pointer.
scopeSeams.data quality: OWNED BY D1 dataqc (gaps, outliers, frozen values, rate while shut in). D4 takes a clean series, refuses a missing month by name, and treats a shut-in month as a real zero.
scopeSeams.Monte Carlo and P labels in general: OWNED BY the uncertainty and dca courses. D4's bootstrap is the residual bootstrap of one method; its labels follow lib/conventions/percentile.js and are taught as the platform convention.
scopeSeams.feature regression: The plan roster (Suite NextGen-Remaining-Courses-PLAN.md section 15) lists feature regression for D4; the engine does not build it (digest section 24, what is not built), and regression is D2's. Open question for the lead.

namingCollisions.forecast: the point forecast of one fitted method; a one-step forecast is a fitted value; a percentile is named as a percentile. Section 25.
namingCollisions.error: actual minus forecast; positive means the forecast was low; a residual is an in-sample one-step error. Sections 11, 25.
namingCollisions.P90: the low case, the 10th percentile of the simulated paths, by exceedance; P10 the high case. Sections 19, 25.
namingCollisions.accuracy: a named metric on named months (in-sample, hold-out, or a backtest with its origins). Section 25.
namingCollisions.trend: the smoothed trend state b. Section 25.
namingCollisions.machine learning: names the method (exponential smoothing, residual bootstrap, least-squares Arps). Section 25.

openItems.ENGINE FINDING E1 (CLOSED, repaired in e: The backtest and compareWithArps MASE labels now read "the training window" once: "MASE is undefined: at origin 12 the training window has 12 values, so the lag-12 naive forecast has no in-sample error (it needs more than 12)" (digest section 3). Was: backtest and compareWithArps build naiveScale's label as `the ${o} training values`, so a training window of m values or fewer reads "MASE is undefined: at origin 12 the 12 training values has 12 values, so the lag-12 naive forecast has no in-sample error (it needs more than 12)" (digest section 3, the notes table): a plural subject with "has", and the count said twice. Reported to the lead; the digest quotes it verbatim until the engine is repaired and the wave re-cut.
openItems.ENGINE FINDING E2 (CLOSED, repaired in e: The zero-scale reason now reads "MASE is undefined: at origin 6 the training window has 6 values and the lag-1 naive forecast has zero in-sample error on them (every y[t] - y[t - 1] is 0), so the scale is 0" (digest sections 3 and 16). Was: the zero-scale reason in a backtest reads "on the 6 values of the 6 training values" (digest section 3 and section 16), the count said twice. Reported to the lead.
openItems.ENGINE FINDING E3 (CLOSED, repaired in e: Singular forms now: "then 1 actual", "leaves no actual" at horizon 1, "1 value", "1 scored residual", "1 path"; the Arps refusal reads "the training window has 2 positive values". Was: checkBacktest writes `then ${horizon} actuals` and `leaves fewer than ${horizon} actuals` with no singular, so horizon 1 reads "then 1 actuals" (digest section 3, the EKENE-P6 backtest refusal) and "leaves fewer than 1 actuals". Reported to the lead.
openItems.ENGINE OBSERVATION E4 (CLOSED, stated in: The bootstrap basis now ends: "residuals are drawn as fitted without centring (their mean is not subtracted), so a method whose residuals have a non-zero mean drifts: on a declining well a flat method's paths can fall below its own point forecast". Digest section 18 quotes it (a must() pins it) and teaches it on ses EKENE-P1. Was: forecastIntervals resamples the residuals as fitted, never centred, so on a declining well a flat method's paths drift and the point forecast can lie outside its own P90 to P10 band (digest section 18: ses on EKENE-P1 at step 12, 211.400000 against a P10 of 69.250000). The basis says the residuals are drawn from the scored in-sample residuals but not that they are uncentred. The course teaches it as a property; the lead may want one clause in the basis and a line in FINDINGS known limits.
openItems.PLAN ROSTER: feature regression: Suite NextGen-Remaining-Courses-PLAN.md section 15 lists 'feature regression' for D4; the engine builds none and the digest lists it as not built, with regression owned by D2. The lead decides whether the roster line is amended.
